title: A Drone Strike on Iraq's Khor Mor Gas Field Blacks Out the Kurdish Region, Blackstone Leads a $3.1B LNG Canada Deal, and Iraq's 5M Bpd Claim Complicates OPEC Talks
subhead: An unmanned aerial attack forced a shutdown at northern Iraq's Khor Mor gas facility and cut electricity to more than 70 percent of the Kurdish region, even as crude futures slipped at the Monday open after President Trump called fresh US strikes on Iran 'unlikely.' Elsewhere, Saudi Aramco launched an expansion to bring its East-West pipeline to 12 million barrels per day within three weeks, Iraqi Oil Minister Basim Mohammed Khudair claimed output above 5 million barrels per day ahead of OPEC+ quota talks, and Blackstone led a $3.1 billion investment in Mitsubishi's stake in LNG Canada.

sections.heading: Drone Strike Shuts Iraq's Khor Mor Gas Field while Oil Slips on Trump's Iran Remarks
sections.body:
An explosive drone struck the Khor Mor gas field in northern Iraq's Sulaymaniyah province late Sunday, forcing operators to suspend gas production and triggering a grid collapse that left more than 70 percent of Iraq's Kurdish region without electricity (Al Jazeera, Star, Yeni Şafak). In Saudi Arabia, an administrative building belonging to Saudi Aramco in Riyadh sustained damage following an attack, even as Aramco announced it had begun expansion work on its strategic East-West Crude Oil Pipeline to reach its maximum capacity of 12 million barrels per day within less than three weeks, bypassing the Strait of Hormuz toward the Red Sea (Bloomberg HT).

Despite the infrastructure strikes, global crude oil futures fell at Monday's open after US President Donald Trump said fresh American military strikes on Iran were 'unlikely' and noted that peace efforts were continuing alongside Task Force 'Iron Gate' (Reuters, Wall Street Journal, Al Jazeera). Meanwhile, elevated jet fuel prices continue to hit Asia-Pacific aviation: Australian flag carrier Qantas projected a first-half fuel bill of $2.63 billion amid wartime oil volatility (Wall Street Journal).
sections.whyItMatters: Saudi Aramco's push to lift East-West pipeline capacity to 12 million barrels a day within three weeks is a direct physical hedge against Hormuz mine and blockade disruptions.

sections.heading: Iraq's 5 Million Bpd Production Claim Complicates Its Push for a Higher OPEC+ Quota
sections.body:
Iraq's campaign to secure a higher baseline production quota from OPEC+ ran into turbulence after Iraqi Oil Minister Basim Mohammed Khudair stated that the country is already producing more than 5 million barrels per day — over 500,000 barrels per day above its current OPEC+ ceiling (OilPrice). Khudair's statement raises compliance questions inside the producer group just weeks after OPEC+ agreed to freeze December output hikes.

In North America, private equity giant Blackstone is leading a $3.1 billion investment to acquire a stake in Mitsubishi Corp.'s interest in the LNG Canada export terminal project in British Columbia, while US natural gas futures posted a modest uptick and Canada's federal budget delivered new tax and funding support for Saskatchewan helium production (Wall Street Journal, Pipeline Online). In Turkey, the Savings Deposit Insurance Fund (TMSF) put LPG storage terminals across Hatay and Giresun belonging to three trusteeship-held companies up for sale at an estimated value of 3.21 billion Turkish lira (Ekonomim).
sections.whyItMatters: By publicly stating it is pumping more than 5 million barrels per day, Baghdad undermines its own argument for a higher official OPEC+ quota by confirming it is already busting its current target by half a million barrels a day.

sections.heading: China Plans $940B Energy Spend in 2026 as COP31 Opens in Antalya and Democrats Eye Clean Energy
sections.body:
As delegations from 196 nations opened the COP31 climate conference in Antalya, Turkey, on Monday, the China Enterprise Reform and Development Society released its 2026 Global Energy Transition Report projecting that China will invest a record $940 billion in its energy sector in 2026 (Bloomberg HT, Yeni Şafak). Highlighting investor appetite for Chinese grid hardware, shares of Chinese battery and energy storage developer RelyEZ jumped on their Hong Kong Stock Exchange debut on Monday, even as China's October producer price index climbed 5.7 percent on higher energy input costs (CNA, Financial Times, Bloomberg). In Antalya, Turkey's VakıfBank announced plans to sign $1.7 billion in new international financing agreements during COP31 to fund renewable energy, energy efficiency, and SME green transition projects, while Japanese Ambassador to Turkey Masami highlighted new bilateral opportunities in hydrogen and energy security (Dünya, Anadolu Agency).

In the United States, Tuesday's Democratic midterm sweep is set to reshuffle energy policy across Congress and key data-center states including Ohio, Georgia, and Texas (OilPrice, AP News). Congressional Democrats announced plans to push clean-energy incentives to lower household utility bills and challenge the White House's fossil-fuel agenda, even as OilPrice noted that Big Oil has become the artificial intelligence industry's favored power partner and countries race to develop space-based solar power (SBSP) and urban waste-heat district networks in New York (AP News, OilPrice).
sections.whyItMatters: While a newly elected Democratic Congress prepares to clash with the White House over clean energy subsidies and data-center power rules, China is deploying nearly $1 trillion a year into domestic energy infrastructure.

sections.heading: Russian Strikes Knock Out Power to 600,000 Ukrainian Homes and Cut Zaporizhzhia Grid Link
sections.body:
Russian missile and drone strikes hit electrical substations in Ukraine's Dnipro and Zhytomyr regions as well as port infrastructure on Sunday, leaving 600,000 households without electricity (Yeni Şafak). Simultaneously, Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha announced that the Russian-held Zaporizhzhia Nuclear Power Plant lost its connection to external power lines for the 16th time this year, forcing reliance on backup systems (Anadolu Agency).

Meanwhile, in global commodities, the World Bank forecast an 18 percent rise in food commodity prices over 2026–2027 driven by energy-linked fertilizer costs, transport disruptions, and extreme weather, while mining equipment analysts projected sustained growth in the global rotary drills market through 2035 on rising critical-minerals capital expenditure (CEO Magazyn, IndexBox).
sections.whyItMatters: The 16th external power loss at Zaporizhzhia this year alongside blackouts for 600,000 Ukrainian households underscores how fragile Eastern Europe's high-voltage grid has become entering winter.

bottomLine: Energy markets opened the week weighing diplomatic calm against physical grid attacks: crude futures dropped after President Trump said new strikes on Iran were 'unlikely,' yet an overnight drone attack shut northern Iraq's Khor Mor gas field and cut power to 70 percent of the Kurdish region while Saudi Aramco raced to expand its East-West pipeline to 12 million barrels per day within three weeks. Within OPEC+, Iraqi Oil Minister Khudair complicated Baghdad's quota lobbying by claiming current output already exceeds 5 million barrels per day. Meanwhile, Blackstone led a $3.1 billion investment in LNG Canada, China projected a record $940 billion energy spend for 2026, and 196 countries opened the COP31 climate summit in Antalya where VakıfBank unveiled a $1.7 billion green financing package.
sources: OilPrice, Wall Street Journal, Financial Times, Reuters, Bloomberg, AP News, Al Jazeera, CNA, SCMP, World Bank, IndexBox, Pipeline Online, Anadolu Agency, Bloomberg HT, Dünya, Ekonomim, Yeni Şafak, Star
